events.excerpt: Elephants live in some of the most complex and resilient societies in the animal kingdom. Individuals die or move away, calves grow up, and newcomers join, but the local communities as a whole usually hold together. Long-term studies of African savanna elephants have shown that, even after poaching or other spikes in deaths, survivors tend to rebuild their lost connections over time. But a new study suggests that resilience may not keep the community intact when steady losses accumulate over time. Anastasia Madsen, a behavioral ecologist at the University of California, San Diego, and her colleagues analyzed 12 years of observations of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka. They found that, once losses began to outpace newcomers, the elephants’ society didn’t just get smaller. It fractured. Accidental savanna Udawalawe National Park in southern Sri Lanka was created in the 1970s around a reservoir on one of the country's four major rivers. “Before that, it was basically a tropical deciduous forest,” said Shermin de Silva, an ecologist at UC San Diego and senior author of the study (de Silva started the Udawalawe Elephant Research Project in 2006). Read full article Comments
events.headline: In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

events.excerpt: One of the struggles with vintage computer systems is that many of the ICs in them have no modern-day version that you can just purchase and drop-in. Creating replacements that use modern-day ICs inside has consequently become a popular direction, with [Philip Smart]’s TranZPUter being one such example . Standing for ‘transformable ZPU Computer’, the tranZPUter is transformable in the sense that it features an FPGA or MCU and the initial iteration targeting the ZPU Evo CPU design. This has led to a number of variants of this concept, including a version targeting the Z80 , the 6502 and 6809. These are based around the RP2350B MCU, using its PIO peripheral to great effect. Of these the Motorola 6809 is probably the lesser known MPU, having been launched in 1978 as an 8-bit MPU with some 16-bit features that could beat the 6502 in many metrics courtesy of its more advanced hardware. It being more expensive led to it only being used in systems like the TRS-80 Color, Dragon 32/64, SuperPET and a whole range of arcade systems. If you have any of those 6809-based systems and the MPU gave up the ghost, you can drop in the Pico6809 board featuring said RP2350B MCU as well as an ESP32 co-processor. Currently it targets the Dragon 32/64 systems, adding not just a fresh MPU, but also adds v
events.headline: Drop-in Vintage CPU Replacements with the tranZPUter Project

events.excerpt: Over the last month, the number of Large Language Model (LLM) penetration testing and orchestration frameworks has exploded. Just a few weeks ago, ARTEX — an open source agentic penetration testing system that automates offensive security workflows — was the only framework available. In just the last three days, we have seen over 50 framework families attempt to scan Cloudflare customers globally. The number of Internet Protocol (IP) addresses seen running these frameworks has grown into the thousands and continues to increase daily. The proliferation of these frameworks has significantly changed the status quo in cyber defense: defenders are struggling to keep up with the volumetric nature of these autonomously guided attacks. ARTEX was taken down by its creator Autumn-27 on October 8. (“The malicious exploitation of this tool runs entirely counter to its original intent,” they wrote in Chinese. ) But in the month since, the ecosystem has exploded with new fragmented versions of it. There are now over 12,000 repositories, with several hundred unique forks containing lineage from the original repository. Additionally, hundreds of other similar agentic orchestration frameworks have been created since October 8. Daily requests of AI penetration testing (pentesting) and exploitation
events.headline: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model

events.excerpt: Overview Important This is a recommended release for all op-challenger operators. It updates dependencies, the Go toolchain and the image's base packages to fix vulnerabilities that image scanners can report against v1.11.0, including CVE-2026-116591 , CVE-2026-84243 and GHSA-53rm-773f-4q8c . None of the vulnerable code is reachable in op-challenger, cannon or kona-host, and there are no other operator-visible changes. Other changes Security github.com/klauspost/compress is updated from v1.18.7 to v1.20.2, fixing CVE-2026-116591 ( GHSA-fpmh-frq8-7rj8 ), a panic in its zstd decoder on two-block frames. op-challenger uses that decoder only to read the superchain registry built into the binary, so no external input reaches it ( #23965 ) The image's glibc-2.44 and libcrypt1-2.44 packages move from 2.44-r9 to 2.44-r18 , which fixes CVE-2026-84243 in libcrypt1 (fixed in 2.44-r16 ). The fixed packages come from rebuilding the image; no code changed op-challenger and cannon are built with Go 1.26.11, whose security fixes include CVE-2026-97054 in net/http . Neither binary serves an HTTP handler wrapped in MaxBytesReader or MaxBytesHandler , so neither was exposed. The other fixes are build-time cgo issues quinn-proto is updated from 0.11.16 to 0.11.19 in the Rust lockfile, clearing GHSA-

events.excerpt: Instead of delivering a strong rebound from the disappointing October, November has offered nothing but more pain for Bitcoin investors. The asset’s price briefly plunged to a three-month low of around $67,600 before recovering to the current $69,300 (per CoinGecko), a 10% weekly decline. As expected, the red wave has weighed on community sentiment, and the popular BTC Fear and Greed Index entered “extreme fear” territory. This may sound scary at first sight, but can it actually be good news? Darkest Before the Dawn? US inflation came in higher than expected, giving the Fed a solid reason to increase interest rates next month. Nvidia’s shares nosedived after its longtime CEO, Jensen Huang, resigned amid an extramarital affairs scandal, triggering a broader sell-off across tech and crypto markets. These are some of the negative headlines that have rattled BTC and the altcoins over the past few days. And since crypto market behavior is very emotional, so are the participants in it. The latest negative events and Bitcoin’s price decline have taken their toll on the Fear and Greed Index, which measures overall sentiment on a scale from 0 (“extreme fear”) to 100 (“extreme greed”).
